transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Well… what brings me in is that I keep hearing these voices, and they’re not vague exactly, they’re clear. It’s mostly in my apartment, when I’m alone, but it’s happened in empty museum rooms too, which is especially unsettling because those rooms have that echo and stillness already.

They sound like women whispering, almost like they’re behind the walls or just out of sight, and they’ll say things about which photographs belong in the archive. Not just random noise — it feels directed, like they’re commenting or instructing me about where things should go. I know that probably sounds strange, but it’s been happening enough that I felt I couldn’t just keep explaining it away.
Do you believe these voices are coming from real women who are actually there?

I don’t usually see anyone there, no. That’s part of what makes it so upsetting. It’s not like I turn and there’s a woman standing in the room talking to me. It’s more like the voices are coming from just behind something — behind the apartment walls, or from the far side of an empty museum room where nobody should be.

But in the moment, they do feel very real. They’re clear enough that I’ll stop what I’m doing and listen, because they sound like women whispering about the photographs, about which ones belong in the archive or where they should go. I know that sounds unlikely when I say it out loud, and I do try to tell myself, “There isn’t anyone here.” But when it’s happening, it doesn’t feel like my imagination. It feels like someone is there, just out of sight.
How long have you been hearing these voices?

It’s been… about eight months now, I think. I didn’t mark it on a calendar at first, because at the beginning I kept thinking maybe I’d misheard something, or maybe it was the building, or someone in the hallway. But when I look back, yes, it’s around eight months that the voices have been happening.

And it’s not just one isolated time and then nothing. Over those months, it’s also gone along with this feeling — really more than a feeling sometimes — that people are watching my archive, paying attention to what I’m doing with it. That certainty has been there for about the same length of time, maybe it grew in around the voices, but roughly eight months.
Do you believe people are watching your archive?

Yes. I do. I know that sounds… I know how it sounds, but yes, I believe they are watching it. Not just in a casual way, not like someone glancing at a website or asking about a donation box. I mean monitoring it — paying attention to what I’m collecting, what I’m organizing, what I’m preparing to show.

It feels very clear to me that the museum board and some of the city arts people know the archive matters. They know my Caribbean archive would change how the galleries tell the truth, because there are photographs and records in it that don’t fit the neat little story they like to present. And I think that’s why they’ve been monitoring my phone, because how else would they know certain things? How else would there be that feeling of being… tracked, almost, around the archive?

And nobody has shown me anything that proves otherwise. People tell me, “Oh, they’re busy,” or “That’s not how institutions work,” but that isn’t proof. That’s just reassurance. It doesn’t answer the fact that they seem to know, or that they’re circling around it. So yes, I believe people are watching my archive.
Did these voices start after any illness, head injury, seizure, or other medical problem?

I don’t think so… at least, nothing that I connected to it. I didn’t have some clear thing where I hit my head and then suddenly the voices started the next day, or anything like that. No one said, “Oh, this is because of a seizure,” or some illness. Not that I know of.

I mean, I’m 64, so of course there are days when you feel run down or your body does strange things and you wonder what’s age and what’s stress and what’s something else. But I can’t point to a medical problem that came first and then the voices followed. It felt more like they just… began showing up, and at first I kept trying to explain them in ordinary ways. The building, someone nearby, maybe I was tired. But not a head injury or seizure that I’m aware of.
Have there been times during this when you felt confused about where you were or what was happening around you?

I don’t think so… not in the way you mean, I don’t think. I haven’t had times where I suddenly didn’t know I was in my apartment, or didn’t recognize the street, or looked around and thought, “Where am I?” At least nothing like that stands out to me.

There are moments when I get overwhelmed, and I’ll be so focused on what’s happening around the archive or trying to make sense of things that everything feels… intense, like I’m trying to track too many pieces at once. But that feels different from being confused about where I am. I know where I am. I know what I’m doing.

Sometimes I might lose the thread of a conversation because I’m distracted or because I’m listening carefully, but I wouldn’t call it not knowing what’s happening around me. If you mean disoriented, then no, I don’t think I’ve had that.
During these past eight months, have you had a period when you felt unusually high, energized, or full of ideas?

Yes… yes, I have. Not all the time, but there are days — stretches, sometimes — where I feel almost lit up from the inside, like everything suddenly connects and I can see what I’m meant to do. I feel radiant, that’s the word I keep coming back to. Like I’ve been chosen for something, like the archive isn’t just a project, it’s… it’s my purpose, and the ideas come so quickly and clearly that it feels impossible that anyone else can’t see it too.

And when I’m in that state, I don’t feel tired of it. I feel pushed forward by it, energized, like I could keep explaining and arranging and planning because it all matters so much. It feels beautiful at first. Powerful, even.

But then if someone questions me — if they say, “Maybe slow down,” or “Are you sure?” or they act like I’m being too much — I get furious. Not just annoyed. Furious. It feels like they’re trying to erase me, like they’re trying to take the meaning away from what I’m doing and make me small again. And I know people may think they’re being reasonable, but in the moment it feels like an attack. Like they’re trying to dim the light just when I finally have it.
When you feel that radiant, energized way, do you need less sleep than usual?

Yes. Very much, actually. When I’m in that radiant state, sleep starts to feel almost… optional, like an inconvenience. I can sleep two or three hours and then wake up before dawn, completely awake, not groggy the way I normally would be. It’s like my eyes open and I’m already ready, already thinking about what needs to be done.

And I tell myself, honestly, that sleep is for people who don’t have an archive to rescue. That sounds dramatic when I say it out loud, but in the moment it feels true. It feels like there’s work waiting for me and I’ve been given this burst of energy for a reason, so why would I waste it lying there? So yes, I need much less sleep then — or at least I feel like I do.
Have there been times when the voices continued even when your mood felt normal—not especially energized or unusually low?

Yes… that did happen. That’s part of what makes it hard for me to explain it as just being tied to those radiant periods, because there was a stretch — I think several weeks — when I wasn’t feeling especially high or full of grand purpose. I wasn’t walking around feeling chosen in that bright, charged way I described. I was more… ordinary, I guess. Not wonderful, not terribly low either. Just myself, or what felt closer to myself.

But the whispers were still there in the apartment. Not constant every second, but enough that I would stop what I was doing and listen, because I was sure I’d heard something. Like low voices just beyond the wall, or coming from a corner where there shouldn’t have been anyone. And even though my mood wasn’t especially elevated then, I still believed the arts people were monitoring my phone. I remember checking it, holding it, thinking, “They’re listening through this,” or that they were tracking what I was saying or doing.

So yes, the voices and that feeling of being watched or monitored didn’t only happen when I was energized. There was definitely a period when my mood felt more normal, but those things were still going on.
During these past eight months, have you had a period of at least two weeks when you felt depressed most of the day nearly every day?

I’m… not sure I can say that clearly. I’ve had low days, yes, and times where everything felt heavy and I didn’t want to deal with people or decisions, but “at least two weeks” and “most of the day nearly every day” — I don’t know. I don’t want to just say yes if I can’t really place it.

My memory of the past months is a little uneven, and sometimes the days blur together. There were stretches where I felt very worn down, but I’m not sure if that was depression in the way you mean, or if it was more exhaustion, discouragement, being overwhelmed. I can remember feeling sad or flattened at times, but I can’t confidently point to a full two-week period where I was depressed most of every day.

So… I suppose the honest answer is I don’t know. I haven’t tracked it that way.
Have you ever had a time when you felt depressed nearly every day for at least two weeks?

I don’t know that I can answer that with a clean yes or no. I’ve had times in my life when I was very down, and I can remember stretches where getting through the day felt heavy, but when you say “nearly every day for at least two weeks,” I start second-guessing myself.

I don’t keep track in that kind of calendar way, and afterward the days sort of compress together in my mind. I can say I’ve felt depressed at times, definitely, but I’m not sure I can honestly say whether it lasted nearly every day for a full two weeks. I wouldn’t want to tell you yes just because it seems like the expected answer.
Before these past eight months began, had you ever had another time in your life when you needed much less sleep than usual and still felt full of energy?

Yes… yes, I have had that before. Not just recently. There have been times earlier in my life where I would sleep maybe two or three hours, and then I’d wake up before dawn as if someone had switched on a light inside me. I wouldn’t feel groggy or like I needed to go back to bed. I’d feel completely ready, almost relieved that the night was over and I could get back to what I thought I needed to do.

And at the time I didn’t think of it as a problem. I would tell myself that sleep was for people who didn’t have an archive to rescue — that sounds strange saying it out loud now, but that was really how it felt. Like there was this urgent work, something important I had to preserve or sort through or save, and sleeping more would have been almost irresponsible.

So yes, there were periods before these past eight months where needing very little sleep didn’t make me tired. I felt energized from it, or at least I believed I was functioning better that way.
Was there ever a period of at least two weeks when you were hearing the voices while not feeling unusually energized or depressed?

Yes… I think there was. I’m trying to be careful with the timing, but yes, there was a stretch of several weeks where I wasn’t feeling especially energized or grand or anything like that. I wasn’t in that state where I felt driven or lit up, and I also don’t remember being especially depressed in the way you were asking about earlier.

But the voices — or whispers, really — were still there. Mostly in the apartment. It would be like low whispering, not always clear enough to make out, but enough that I felt certain someone was there or that something was being said about me. And during that same period I still believed the arts people were monitoring my phone. That didn’t go away just because my mood was more ordinary.

So yes, if you’re asking whether the voices and that belief continued when I wasn’t unusually up or deeply down, I would say yes. That did happen for several weeks.
Did the voices continue for at least two weeks during a time when you were not feeling unusually energized or depressed?

Yes, they did. I know I already sort of said this, but yes — there was a stretch that was more than just a few days. It was several weeks, as best as I can place it, where I wasn’t feeling unusually energized or big or grand, and I wasn’t in one of those very low states either.

I was more… ordinary, mood-wise, I guess. But the whispers were still happening in the apartment. Not always loud, not always words I could make out, but enough that I would stop what I was doing and listen, because it felt like someone was there or talking just out of reach.

And the thing with the arts people monitoring my phone was still very real to me then. That belief didn’t shut off just because my mood wasn’t extreme. So yes, the voices continued for at least two weeks during a time when I wasn’t unusually energized or depressed.
Have you ever had a period of at least two weeks when you felt depressed most of the day nearly every day?

I’m not sure I can answer that cleanly. I mean, I’ve had times where I felt very low, yes, but when you say “most of the day nearly every day” and for two whole weeks, I get a little tangled trying to measure it that way.

There were days when I felt heavy and slowed down, like everything took too much effort, but I don’t know if I could honestly say it was nearly every day for at least two weeks. My memory of it isn’t organized like that — it’s more like patches, or stretches, but I don’t want to say yes if I’m not certain.

So… I guess my answer is I don’t know. I’ve had depressed periods, but I’m not sure they fit exactly what you’re asking.
At any time in your life, have you had delusions or heard voices for at least two weeks when you were not feeling unusually high or depressed?

Yes. I know I’ve said parts of this already, but yes, there was a period like that. It wasn’t just one bad night or a couple of strange days. It went on for several weeks, as best as I can remember.

During that time, I wasn’t feeling unusually high or energized. I wasn’t feeling grand, or like I had some special drive, or like everything was speeding up. And I also wasn’t especially depressed in the way you mean — not that deep, all-day kind of low. My mood was more… normal for me, I guess.

But the whispers were still there in the apartment. They would come when I was just doing ordinary things, and I’d stop and listen because it really felt like someone was there, or like people were talking just out of sight. And I was still convinced the arts people were monitoring my phone. That belief didn’t go away during that quieter mood period.

So yes — I did have at least two weeks, really several weeks, where the voices and that belief were still happening even though I wasn’t unusually high or depressed.
Have you had any recent changes in your medications?

I’m not completely sure how to answer that, because I don’t keep track of the medication details as neatly as I probably should. I don’t want to tell you something wrong.

As far as I know, there haven’t been any big recent changes that I can clearly point to, but I’d have to look at the bottles or my notes to be certain. Sometimes the names and doses blur together for me, especially if it’s been adjusted before, so I don’t want to guess and make it sound more definite than it is.
Have you ever been diagnosed with a neurological illness, such as epilepsy, Parkinson’s disease, or dementia?

I don’t think so. Not that I’ve been told, anyway.

I mean, no doctor has sat me down and said I have epilepsy or Parkinson’s or dementia, at least not that I remember. I’ve had different doctors over the years, and sometimes the appointments blur together, so I don’t want to sound like I’m giving you a perfectly organized medical history. But as far as I know, no, I haven’t been diagnosed with a neurological illness like that.

If there’s something specific you’re looking for, I can try to think it through, but I don’t have a known diagnosis like those.
Have you used any drugs or substances that can affect the mind, such as cannabis, cocaine, methamphetamine, or hallucinogens?

I’m not sure how to answer that in a precise way. I don’t think I have anything clear to tell you there.

I mean, I know what you’re asking — things like cannabis or harder drugs or hallucinogens — but I don’t want to just give a confident-sounding answer if I’m not thinking of every possible thing. As far as I know, I haven’t been using anything like that recently, or anything that I would think of as mind-affecting in that way.

If you mean prescribed medicines or over-the-counter things too, that’s a little different, and I’d probably need to look at what I actually take. But for drugs like the ones you listed, I don’t have a specific substance use thing to report.
Have you ever had a time when you felt depressed nearly every day for two weeks and also lost interest or pleasure in things you usually care about?

I’m not completely sure how to pin that down. I’ve had low periods, definitely, but when you say “nearly every day for two weeks” and also “lost interest or pleasure,” I get a little tangled trying to be exact.

I can remember times where I didn’t feel like myself and things felt kind of flat, but I don’t know if I could honestly say it was every day for a full two weeks, or that I lost interest in everything I usually care about. Sometimes I still do things out of habit even if I don’t enjoy them much, so it’s hard for me to separate “not interested” from just being tired or withdrawn.

So I guess my answer is: I’m not sure. I don’t want to say yes if it wasn’t really that pattern, but I also don’t want to say no like nothing like that has ever happened. I’d probably need help walking through the timing.
